passages.text:
Clement to James, the lord and bishop of bishops, who governs the holy Jerusalem church of the Hebrews and the churches everywhere that have been well established by God’s providence, together with the elders and deacons and all the other brothers: may peace always be.

Let it be known to you, my lord, that Simon—who, because of his true faith and the surest basis of his teaching, was designated to be the foundation of the church and, for this very reason, was renamed Peter by Jesus himself with his unlying mouth; the firstfruits of our Lord; the first of the apostles; the one to whom the Father first revealed the Son; the one whom the Messiah rightly pronounced blessed; the called and chosen one, table companion and fellow traveler; the good and proven disciple; the one commanded to enlighten the West, the darker part of the world, as more capable than everyone else, and who proved able to accomplish it—and indeed, how long shall I prolong the account, unwilling to disclose the painful thing that necessity compels me, even if late, in any event to tell? This same man, because of his boundless affection for humanity, clearly and publicly announced to the whole world, before the evil one now in power, the good king who was to come. Having come as far as this place, Rome, and saving people through teaching willed by God, he himself, through violence, exchanged life in the present existence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the holy Jerusalem church of the Hebrews
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Jerusalem as the church’s location or identifying designation and retains the explicit association with the Hebrews.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν ἀσφαλεστάτην αὐτοῦ τῆς διδασκαλίας ὑπόθεσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the surest basis of his teaching
lexical_decisions.rationale: Here ὑπόθεσις denotes the underlying basis or foundation of the teaching, while the superlative force of ἀσφαλεστάτην is retained.

lexical_decisions.chosen: with his unlying mouth
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the source’s concrete image and its claim that Jesus’ naming was free from falsehood.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Χριστός functions independently as a title here rather than as part of the name Jesus Christ.

lexical_decisions.chosen: before the evil one now in power
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats πονηροῦ as a personal evil ruler and ἐνεστῶτος as describing his present ascendancy; the phrase could also be understood more generally as ‘amid the present evil.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: through teaching willed by God
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders the compound θεοβούλητος as teaching that accords with or proceeds from God’s will.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ νῦν βίου βιαίως τὸ ζῆν μετήλλαξεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: through violence, exchanged life in the present existence
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the exchange/departure language of μεταλλάσσω and the explicit claim that the death was violent.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ· μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ;
source_issues.issue: The printed high point after μέχρι ποῦ interrupts the interrogative phrase from its verb μηκύνω and leaves the exact scope of the question editorially uncertain. The translation treats the words as one rhetorical question; this is a proposed repunctuation, not a change to the supplied transcription.
source_issues.proposed_reading: καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ;

passages.text: Now, in the very days when he was about to die, after the brothers had assembled, he suddenly took hold of my hand, stood up in the assembly, and said, “Listen to me, brothers and fellow servants. Since—as I was taught by the Lord and Teacher Jesus Christ, who sent me—the days of my death have drawn near, I ordain this Clement as bishop for you. To him I entrust my teaching chair. He accompanied me from the beginning to the end and thus listened to all my discourses; to sum it up, he shared in all my trials and was found persevering in faith. More than all the others, I have found by experience that he is God-revering, a lover of humanity, pure, widely learned, self-controlled, good, just, patient, and knows how to bear bravely the ingratitude of some of those receiving instruction. Therefore I impart to him the authority to bind and release, so that whatever he decrees on earth will stand decreed in the heavens. For he will bind what must be bound and release what must be released, since he knows the church’s rule. Listen to him, therefore, recognizing that whoever grieves the one who presides over truth sins against the Messiah and provokes the Father of all; because of this, that person will not live. And so the one who presides must himself occupy the place of a physician, not possess the rage of an irrational beast.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: fellow servants
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the shared servant status expressed by the compound rather than reducing it to a general term for colleagues.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ᾧ τὴν ἐμὴν τῶν λόγων πιστεύω καθέδραν
lexical_decisions.chosen: To him I entrust my teaching chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: Καθέδρα is retained through the institutional image of a chair, while τῶν λόγων identifies it as the office of authoritative teaching.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a lover of humanity
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the word’s explicit orientation toward human beings rather than narrowing it to generic kindness.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those receiving instruction
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys the participle’s sense without requiring the later technical loanword ‘catechumens.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: to bind and release
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the paired judicial and disciplinary imagery; ‘release’ distinguishes λύειν from merely untying a physical object.

lexical_decisions.chosen: whatever he decrees
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this construction χειροτονέω concerns an authoritative determination about a matter, not the ordination of a person.

lexical_decisions.chosen: whoever grieves the one who presides over truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the act of causing grief and the image of occupying the leading seat in relation to truth.

lexical_decisions.chosen: occupy the place of a physician
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the source’s contrast between healing pastoral authority and the rage of a beast.

passages.text: As he was saying these things, I fell before him and pleaded with him, declining the honor and authority of the chair. But he answered, “Do not petition me about this, for I have resolved that this should happen—and all the more so if you decline it—because such a chair does not need a rash man eager to occupy the chair, but one who is circumspect in character and widely learned in discourse. Present someone better, one who accompanied me longer than you, listened to my words, and thoroughly learned the governance of the church, and I will not force you to act rightly against your will. But you will not now be able to produce anyone better than yourself, for through me you are the choicest firstfruits of the nations being saved. Nevertheless, consider this other point as well: if, fearing the danger of sin, you do not undertake the governance of the church, know well that you sin more, since, though able to help God-revering people who are like those sailing in peril, you refuse, looking only to what is your own and not to what benefits everyone in common. I know with certainty that you must in every case undertake the danger, since I do not cease asking this of you for the help of everyone. Therefore, the sooner you agree with me, the more you will relieve me of discouragement.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: παραιτούμενος τὴν τῆς καθέδρας τιμήν τε καὶ ἐξουσίαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: declining the honor and authority of the chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Clement’s refusal of both the office’s prestige and its governing power.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a rash man eager to occupy the chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys the coined expression’s criticism of someone ambitious for the presiding seat.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εὐλαβοῦς τὸν τρόπον καὶ πολυμαθοῦς τὸν λόγον
lexical_decisions.chosen: circumspect in character and widely learned in discourse
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context contrasts reckless ambition with cautious character and extensive competence in teaching.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Present someone better
lexical_decisions.rationale: The imperative challenges Clement to identify a more qualified alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the choicest firstfruits
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses idiomatic English to retain the comparative evaluation attached to the firstfruits metaphor.

lexical_decisions.chosen: like those sailing in peril
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the maritime image rather than reducing it to a general statement about danger.

lexical_decisions.chosen: what benefits everyone in common
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the contrast between Clement’s private interest and the community’s shared good.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you agree with me
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound describes Clement joining Peter in approving and accepting the proposed course.

source_issues.issue: The supplied print places a full stop immediately after the elided δ᾽, syntactically separating ὁ δ᾽ from ἀπεκρίνατο. This appears to be an editorial punctuation blemish rather than missing text; the translation reads the words continuously.

passages.text: “I myself know, Clement, that in giving you griefs, discouragements, dangers, and reproaches from uneducated crowds, I am presenting you with gifts. You will be able to bear them bravely by keeping in view the great reward from God that will be repaid to you for your endurance. But also, as is right, consider together with me: when does the Messiah need your alliance—now, when the evil one has taken up war against his bride, or in the coming time, when, having conquered, he reigns and no longer needs any help? Is it not clear even to someone with little understanding that it is now? Therefore, with all your resolve, hurry to ally yourself in this present time of need with a good king, who is naturally disposed to repay great rewards after victory. Gladly, then, serve as bishop—all the more suitably for this reason, since you have learned from me how to govern a church—for the salvation of the brothers who take refuge with us.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: I am presenting you with gifts
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the deliberately paradoxical portrayal of suffering and criticism as gifts.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐνορῶν τῆς ὑπομονῆς τὸν ἐκ θεοῦ σοι μέγαν ἀποδιδόμενον μισθόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: keeping in view the great reward from God that will be repaid to you for your endurance
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the visual orientation of ἐνορῶν and the recompense language of μισθός and ἀποδίδωμι.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Χριστός functions independently as the title of the king whose cause Clement is urged to support.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κατὰ τῆς αὐτοῦ νύμφης πόλεμον ἤρατο
lexical_decisions.chosen: has taken up war against his bride
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps both the military action and the bride image without identifying the bride more explicitly than the source does.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Therefore, with all your resolve
lexical_decisions.rationale: Προαίρεσις here denotes deliberate commitment or resolve, strengthened by πάσῃ.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to ally yourself with a good king
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the political and military alliance imagery rather than generalizing it as mere assistance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Gladly, then, serve as bishop
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb directly calls Clement to perform episcopal oversight and carries a word-family connection with his appointment as ἐπίσκοπος.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the brothers who take refuge with us
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the directional and protective force of προσφεύγω.

source_issues.source_quote: μισθοὺς μεγάλους· μετὰ νίκην ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι
source_issues.issue: The printed high point places a strong editorial pause between the object μισθοὺς μεγάλους and the infinitive ἀποδιδόναι on which it depends. The syntax remains recoverable, and the translation reads the phrase continuously; the proposed reading is conjectural repunctuation only.
source_issues.proposed_reading: μισθοὺς μεγάλους μετὰ νίκην ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι

passages.text: “Nevertheless, before everyone and for everyone’s sake, I also wish to remind you briefly about the matters of governance. You must live blamelessly and, with the greatest diligence, shake off all the occupations of ordinary life, becoming neither a guarantor nor an advocate and entangling yourself in no other worldly affair. For the Messiah does not want you appointed as a judge and arbiter of financial or business matters among the worldly affairs of the present, so that, absorbed in people’s present concerns, you have no leisure to separate, by the word of truth, the better people from the worse. Rather, let those who are learning provide these services for one another, and let them not distract you from the words capable of saving. For just as it is impious for you to undertake worldly concerns while abandoning what you were commanded to do, so it is a sin for each layperson if they do not assist one another also in worldly needs. Moreover, if everyone does not understand that they must keep you free from concern about the matters from which you must be free, let them learn it from the deacons, so that you may care only for the church, both governing it well and providing the words of truth.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: before everyone and for everyone’s sake
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes ἐπὶ πάντων as a public setting and διὰ πάντας as expressing the benefit or concern motivating the instruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πάσας τὰς τοῦ βίου ἀσχολίας ἀποσείεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: shake off all the occupations of ordinary life
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the physical force of ἀποσείω and the comprehensive scope of πάσας.

lexical_decisions.chosen: becoming neither a guarantor nor an advocate
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the distinct financial and legal roles prohibited to the bishop.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κριτὴν καὶ δικαστὴν χρημάτων ἢ ἀσχολημάτων
lexical_decisions.chosen: a judge and arbiter of financial or business matters
lexical_decisions.rationale: Distinguishes the two judicial terms while rendering the governed nouns as ordinary financial and business disputes.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: χωρίζειν λόγῳ ἀληθείας ἀνθρώπων τοὺς κρείττονας ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων
lexical_decisions.chosen: to separate, by the word of truth, the better people from the worse
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the source’s language of separation and its comparison between better and worse persons.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those who are learning
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the expression broader than a fixed institutional label such as ‘catechumens.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: for each layperson
lexical_decisions.rationale: Λαϊκός explicitly contrasts ordinary members with the bishop and deacons in the surrounding instructions.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μόνης τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὴν φροντίδα ἔχῃς
lexical_decisions.chosen: you may care only for the church
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the exclusive force of μόνης and the bishop’s assigned sphere of concern.
